title: 265. 5 tips for pursuing your creative passion

sentences.en: This is an iHeart Podcast, Guaranteed Human.
sentences.zh: 这是一档 iHeart 播客，纯粹的人类创作。

sentences.en: I've been approaching my health really differently this year.
sentences.zh: 今年，我对待健康的方式有了很大的改变。

sentences.en: I used to be really focused on maximizing and doing more, and now I'm just realizing that if I listen to what my body needs, I perform way better,
sentences.zh: 过去我总是专注于追求极致和做更多的事情，但现在我意识到，如果我倾听身体的需求，我的表现反而会好得多，

sentences.en: and that's why I am obsessed with my WHOOP.
sentences.zh: 这就是我为什么对 WHOOP 如此着迷的原因。

sentences.en: Truly, you guys, you know I'm such a data and information-driven person, and I love opening my WHOOP app and seeing how my sleep, my stress, my strain
sentences.zh: 说真的，你们知道我是一个非常依赖数据和信息的人，我喜欢打开 WHOOP 应用程序，看看我的睡眠、压力、身体负荷

sentences.en: is correlating with my mood, with my running performance, with how I'm just feeling day-to-day.
sentences.zh: 是如何与我的情绪、跑步表现以及我日常的感受相关联的。

sentences.en: I'm not an elite athlete by any means, but I do really benefit, and I also just really enjoy knowing more about my body.
sentences.zh: 我绝不是什么精英运动员，但我确实从中受益匪浅，而且我也真的很享受去了解自己的身体。

sentences.en: And WHOOP also gives me these actionable, personalized insights that have made me more intentional and meant that I make smarter decisions day-to-day
sentences.zh: WHOOP 还为我提供了这些可操作的、个性化的见解，让我变得更有目标感，也意味着我在日常生活中能做出更明智的决定，

sentences.en: about what I need rather than just putting my foot on the gas and just going, going, going, going.
sentences.zh: 而不是一味地踩油门，只顾着不停地向前冲。

sentences.en: New members can try WHOOP with a 30-day free trial before committing to a membership.
sentences.zh: 新用户可以在订阅会员之前，先通过 30 天的免费试用期来体验 WHOOP。

sentences.en: That's join.whoop.com slash psychology for your free month of WHOOP.
sentences.zh: 访问 join.whoop.com/psychology 即可获得一个月的免费 WHOOP 体验。

sentences.zh: 有没有什么珍贵的物品是你永远不会扔掉的？

sentences.en: A movie ticket, a boarding pass, or maybe something that makes no sense to anyone but you?
sentences.zh: 一张电影票、一张登机牌，或者某种对别人来说毫无意义，但对你却意义非凡的东西？

sentences.en: In the new podcast, Charmed, with Sam Todd,
sentences.zh: 在 Sam Todd 主持的全新播客《Charmed》中，

sentences.en: Sam explores the memories, obsessions, and tiny treasures that become part of who you are.
sentences.zh: Sam 探索了那些成为你生命一部分的记忆、执念和微小的宝藏。

sentences.en: Charmed is warm, it's funny, it's nostalgic, and just full of the little moments and memories that make life matter.
sentences.zh: 《Charmed》温暖、幽默、充满怀旧感，它记录了那些让生活变得有意义的点滴瞬间和回忆。

sentences.en: Charmed, with Sam Todd, stories worn to tell with Pandora.
sentences.zh: 《Charmed》，与 Sam Todd 一起，讲述 Pandora 佩戴出的故事。

sentences.en: Listen now on iHeart.
sentences.zh: 现在就在 iHeart 上收听吧。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, it is so great to have you here back for another episode as we break down the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 无论你是新听众还是老听众，无论你身处世界何方，很高兴你能回来收听新一期节目，我们将继续剖析 20 多岁时的心理状态。

sentences.en: Today, let's cut straight to the chase.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们开门见山。

sentences.en: I want to talk about creative passion projects, creative side hustles, creative hobbies, the things that we are called to deeply create and express and make,
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈创意激情项目、创意副业、创意爱好，那些我们内心深处渴望去创造、表达和完成的事情，

sentences.en: and basically how to find a balance between making time for creation in our busy world and also needing to work, needing to pay our bills.
sentences.zh: 以及在忙碌的世界中，如何在为创作留出时间与维持生计、支付账单之间找到平衡。

sentences.en: How do we find the balance between practicality and passion?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何在现实与激情之间找到平衡？

sentences.en: How can we hold both of these things at once without feeling like our creative endeavors are always the first thing to basically be sacrificed?
sentences.zh: 我们如何才能同时兼顾这两者，而不至于觉得我们的创意追求总是第一个被牺牲掉的？

sentences.en: I get so many questions about this, specifically from obviously people in their 20s who are facing this dilemma of do I pursue the thing that I'm really passionate about,
sentences.zh: 我收到了很多关于这方面的问题，特别是来自那些 20 多岁、正面临这种两难境地的人：我是该追求我真正热衷的事情，

sentences.en: some creative act, some entrepreneurial idea, or do I stick with what is expected of me, what is very traditional, what is very stable?
sentences.zh: 某种创意行为、某种创业想法，还是坚持做那些被期望的、非常传统、非常稳定的事情？

sentences.en: And specifically, the questions I often get are around how we can turn our passions into our jobs, when to take the risk and pursue whatever it is you want to pursue,
sentences.zh: 我经常收到的具体问题是关于如何将激情转化为工作，何时该冒险去追求你想要追求的东西，

sentences.en: art, music, writing, podcasting full time, but also so many DMs asking me for time management strategies, how to deal with creative blocks,
sentences.zh: 比如艺术、音乐、写作、全职做播客，但也有很多人私信我询问时间管理策略，如何应对创作瓶颈，

sentences.en: how to know when financially you are ready to pursue your creative passion full time.
sentences.zh: 以及如何判断自己在经济上是否准备好全职追求创意激情。

sentences.en: So I really thought that it deserved its own episode because I can speak really deeply to this from experience.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这值得专门做一期节目，因为我可以根据自己的经验深入谈谈这一点。

sentences.en: If you are new to the show and you don't know the origin story of the psychology of your 20s, this podcast started all the way back in 2021, so almost four years ago.
sentences.zh: 如果你是新听众，不知道《20 多岁时的心理学》的起源故事，这档播客始于 2021 年，也就是将近四年前。

sentences.en: And when I first started it, I wasn't working.
sentences.zh: 当我刚开始做的时候，我并没有工作。

sentences.en: I was fun employed.
sentences.zh: 我当时处于“快乐失业”状态。

sentences.en: Basically, I was convinced I was going to take a gap year and then I ended up working in a corporate job for around a year and a half, almost two years,
sentences.zh: 基本上，我本来打算休个间隔年，结果后来在一家公司工作了大约一年半，快两年，

sentences.en: whilst I was doing the podcast full time as well.
sentences.zh: 同时我也在全职做播客。

sentences.en: So I was working a full time job and I was putting out this show and I was, I don't know, I don't like to say building the platform.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时有一份全职工作，同时还在制作这个节目，我不知道该怎么说，我不喜欢说“建立平台”这种话。

sentences.en: The show was just growing as I poured more love into it, basically.
sentences.zh: 随着我投入更多的爱，节目自然而然地成长起来了。

sentences.en: And at some point, I had to basically make the decision, do I leave the steadiness and the stability, especially the financial stability, of my full time job for the podcast?
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，我必须做出决定：我是要放弃全职工作的稳定，尤其是经济上的稳定，去全身心投入播客，

sentences.en: Or do I kind of just, you know, continue to make this my side hustle?
sentences.zh: 还是继续把它当作副业？

sentences.en: And I really found that every single day, I was so excited to get home and just work on the podcast and I really didn't care about work anymore and it was just impossible
sentences.zh: 我发现每天下班回家后，我都非常兴奋地去处理播客，我再也不关心工作了，这简直不可能

sentences.en: to hold both of those things at once.
sentences.zh: 同时兼顾这两件事。

sentences.en: So I decided to quit my job and to pursue what, you know, is a creative passion for me.
sentences.zh: 所以我决定辞职，去追求对我来说充满激情的创意事业。

sentences.en: Like podcasting is actually a real creative force and there's so much creativity and inspiration involved in coming up with ideas.
sentences.zh: 播客确实是一种真正的创意力量，在构思想法的过程中涉及大量的创造力和灵感。

sentences.en: I find the research to be quite a fun process.
sentences.zh: 我觉得研究过程本身就非常有趣。

sentences.en: So I want to really talk about what I learned from that experience and how you can maybe take my story and elements of it and apply it to your own journey
sentences.zh: 所以我真的很想谈谈我从那次经历中学到了什么，以及你如何借鉴我的故事和其中的要素，并将其应用到你自己的旅程中，

sentences.en: with your creative project or passion.
sentences.zh: 去实现你的创意项目或激情。

sentences.en: And maybe the goal for you is to make that passion into a full time career.
sentences.zh: 也许你的目标是把那份激情变成全职事业。

sentences.en: Maybe it's not.
sentences.zh: 也许不是。

sentences.en: I think regardless, this episode will have a lot for you.
sentences.zh: 但我认为无论如何，这期节目都会对你有所启发。

sentences.en: I also want to discuss some of the many barriers, hurdles, boundaries that we kind of clash against in this space.
sentences.zh: 我还想讨论我们在这一领域中会遇到的许多障碍、困难和界限。

sentences.en: When we are someone who is creative and passionate about something and doing something quite artistic with our free time,
sentences.zh: 当我们是一个有创造力、对某事充满热情，并利用业余时间进行艺术创作的人时，

sentences.en: you know, there's going to be a lot of loud forces and voices telling you that you can't do it or, you know, voices from within doubting yourself, imposter syndrome,
sentences.zh: 你会听到很多嘈杂的声音告诉你做不到，或者来自内心的自我怀疑、冒名顶替综合症，

sentences.en: artistic blocks, also things like money and time.
sentences.zh: 还有艺术瓶颈，以及金钱和时间等问题。

sentences.en: There is a real limit sometimes onto where our creative passion can take us because of these boundaries and barriers.
sentences.zh: 由于这些界限和障碍，我们的创意激情有时确实会受到限制。

sentences.en: So I really want to use this episode to basically teach you how you can use psychology to take yourself from a place of perfectionism and fear, really to a place of creation
sentences.zh: 所以我真的想利用这期节目来教你如何运用心理学，让自己从完美主义和恐惧中走出来，真正进入一个创造、

sentences.en: and abundance and consistency.
sentences.zh: 丰盛和持续产出的状态。

sentences.en: I'm very, very excited for this episode.
sentences.zh: 我对这期节目感到非常非常兴奋。

sentences.en: Some of the research and the studies surrounding this is just fascinating.
sentences.zh: 围绕这个主题的一些研究和调查简直太迷人了。

sentences.en: There is this whole area of psychological research that is focused on creativity and how we as humans practice it and also on how we make a living out of it and what that does
sentences.zh: 心理学研究中有一个完整的领域专注于创造力，研究我们人类如何实践创造力，以及我们如何以此为生，以及这会对

sentences.en: to the relationship.
sentences.zh: 这种关系产生什么影响。

sentences.en: So there is a lot to look forward to.
sentences.zh: 所以有很多值得期待的内容。

sentences.en: Without further ado, let's get into it.
sentences.zh: 废话不多说，让我们开始吧。

sentences.en: So you want to put your creative passion basically at the center of your life.
sentences.zh: 所以你想把你的创意激情放在生活的中心。

sentences.en: That's probably why you are listening to this podcast and let me just firstly say that is amazing.
sentences.zh: 这可能就是你收听这档播客的原因，首先我要说，这太棒了。

sentences.en: That is amazing.
sentences.zh: 这真的很棒。

sentences.en: I am fully supportive of this decision.
sentences.zh: 我完全支持这个决定。

sentences.en: I don't even know you and I still think it's a great idea.
sentences.zh: 虽然我不认识你，但我仍然认为这是一个伟大的想法。

sentences.en: But before we talk about how to make this possible, let's talk about some of the difficulties that you might encounter or that you probably already have because I think
sentences.zh: 但在我们讨论如何实现这一点之前，先谈谈你可能会遇到，或者可能已经遇到的一些困难，因为我认为

sentences.en: they bear mentioning and let's just get them out of the way.
sentences.zh: 这些问题值得一提，让我们先把它们解决掉。

sentences.en: Let's get the fear part out of the way.
sentences.zh: 让我们把恐惧的部分先抛开。

sentences.en: Another interesting thing that I think we encounter is naysayers.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们遇到的另一个有趣的事情是“唱反调的人”。

sentences.en: Naysayers, people who are pessimistic about your journey, pessimistic about your chances of success.
sentences.zh: 唱反调的人，那些对你的旅程持悲观态度，对你成功的机会持悲观态度的人。

sentences.en: There is always, always going to be someone who does not believe in you, who says that you should be more careful.
sentences.zh: 总会有人不相信你，说你应该更谨慎一些。

sentences.en: You should be more realistic.
sentences.zh: 你应该更现实一些。

sentences.en: Maybe it's a parent, maybe it's a partner.
sentences.zh: 也许是父母，也许是伴侣。

sentences.en: They'll call your ambitions cute or they obviously don't think you're capable.
sentences.zh: 他们会说你的抱负很“可爱”，或者他们显然认为你没有能力。

sentences.en: Maybe it's someone online, someone who calls themselves a friend.
sentences.zh: 也许是网上的某个人，或者是自称朋友的人。

sentences.en: I know that sometimes these people, if we give them the benefit of the doubt, are genuinely worried about you but don't let their doubts become your own.
sentences.zh: 我知道有时这些人，如果我们往好处想，他们是真心担心你，但千万不要让他们的怀疑变成你自己的怀疑。

sentences.en: I think that for every person who does believe in you, there's always going to be that one person who has to voice every concern they have or worse yet, who actively
sentences.zh: 我认为，对于每一个相信你的人，总会有那么一个人非要表达出他们所有的担忧，或者更糟糕的是，他们会积极地

sentences.en: really does try to bring you down.
sentences.zh: 试图打压你。

sentences.en: Truly, you know, gives you all their judgment and makes it your burden and I really want to tell you right now, pay those judgments no mind at all because often, if this is someone
sentences.zh: 说真的，他们把所有的评判都强加给你，让你背负沉重的负担。我真的想现在就告诉你，完全不要理会这些评判，因为通常情况下，如果这是一个

sentences.en: who does not know you or care about you, it is a massive projection and reflection of what they are feeling internally about their own capabilities and their own dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 不了解你也不关心你的人，这只是他们对自己能力和梦想内心感受的投射和反映。

sentences.en: You know, the people who
sentences.zh: 你知道，那些

sentences.en: I've encountered who have the most and the worst things to say and who did have the worst things to say about my own journey to quit my full-time job to do the podcast full-time,
sentences.zh: 我遇到的、说过最多最难听的话的人，以及那些对我辞掉全职工作去全职做播客的旅程说三道四的人，

sentences.en: most of them actually had grand ambitions of their own that they had abandoned and, you know, those are the people who expressed the most doubt about my goals because I think
sentences.zh: 他们中的大多数人其实自己也有过宏大的抱负，但他们放弃了。我认为，正是这些人对我目标的怀疑最深，因为我觉得

sentences.en: somewhere deep down, they kind of wanted me to quit.
sentences.zh: 在内心深处，他们其实希望我也放弃。

sentences.en: They wanted me to join them in this boat, this boat filled with people who, for whatever reason, and many of them were good reasons, but they had given up on their artistic
sentences.zh: 他们想让我加入他们的行列，这艘船上载满了因为各种原因（其中许多原因确实是合理的）而放弃了艺术和

sentences.en: creative dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 创意梦想的人。

sentences.en: So, this idea that naysayers are projecting their own insecurities around their inability to follow their passions, there is proof of this and the proof for this comes from a
sentences.zh: 所以，这种认为“唱反调的人是在投射他们因无法追随激情而产生的不安全感”的观点是有证据的，证据来自

sentences.en: study from the University of Alaska which examined
sentences.zh: 阿拉斯加大学的一项研究，该研究调查了

sentences.en: 210 individuals and found that those who self-reported higher levels of insecurity, they were more likely to openly criticise the work of others and not only were they more
sentences.zh: 210 名个体，发现那些自述不安全感水平较高的人，更有可能公开批评他人的工作，而且不仅是

sentences.en: likely to criticise, their criticisms were harsher than other people's and often, this is the very important part, often the people they were most critical of were those whose work
sentences.zh: 更有可能批评，他们的批评比其他人更严厉，而且通常——这是非常重要的一点——他们最严厉批评的对象，往往是那些他们认为工作

sentences.en: they thought was better than their own.
sentences.zh: 比自己更好的人。

sentences.en: So, this is describing something called ego defence in psychology.
sentences.zh: 所以，这描述了心理学中所谓的“自我防御”。

sentences.en: Sometimes, often we criticise others as a way of protecting our ego from feeling devalued.
sentences.zh: 有时，我们批评他人是为了保护我们的自我，不让自己感到被贬低。

sentences.en: You know, so even if my work sucks, if I can convince myself and convince someone else that their work also sucks and sucks more, well then I won't feel so bad.
sentences.zh: 你知道，即使我的工作很烂，如果我能说服自己和别人说他们的工作更烂，那我就不会感觉那么糟糕了。

sentences.en: Do not listen to them.
sentences.zh: 不要听他们的。

sentences.en: My saying is always prove them wrong with a smile on your face and that is kind of the sweetest revenge.
sentences.zh: 我的座右铭永远是：面带微笑地证明他们错了，这才是最甜蜜的复仇。

sentences.en: I think everyone says you can't until you do and then suddenly they will say that they were your best friend.
sentences.zh: 我想每个人都会说你做不到，直到你做到了，然后突然间他们就会说他们一直是你最好的朋友。

sentences.en: You know, they suddenly have always believed in you but you have to know that you believed in yourself the whole time and you were doing it because you loved it because you felt
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们突然表现得好像一直相信你，但你必须知道，你一直以来都相信自己，你这样做是因为你热爱它，因为你觉得

sentences.en: like you could rise above all of this judgement, all of these doubts and just do it yourself.
sentences.zh: 你可以超越所有的评判、所有的怀疑，亲自去实现它。

sentences.en: So naysayers, that's a big one.
sentences.zh: 所以，唱反调的人，这是一个大问题。

sentences.en: Another big barrier to pursuing our creative passion whether it's full-time or part-time or in our spare time is lacking inspiration or motivation.
sentences.zh: 追求创意激情的另一个巨大障碍，无论是全职、兼职还是在业余时间，就是缺乏灵感或动力。

sentences.en: This is otherwise known as writer's block, creative block, artistic block.
sentences.zh: 这通常被称为“写作瓶颈”、“创意瓶颈”或“艺术瓶颈”。

sentences.en: I think we've all come across this in some capacity.
sentences.zh: 我想我们都以某种方式遇到过这种情况。

sentences.en: You know, you really want to make something, you finally have the time to do it, you've devoted time to your craft, you're sitting down in front of the blank page and nothing is
sentences.zh: 你知道，你真的很想创作点什么，终于有时间去做了，你投入了时间在你的手艺上，你坐在空白的页面前，却什么也

sentences.en: coming to you.
sentences.zh: 想不出来。

sentences.en: So to understand why this happens and why so often we can sit there and say, you know, I just want a big idea, I want to make something huge, I want to have this, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以要理解为什么会发生这种情况，以及为什么我们经常坐在那里说：“我只是想要一个伟大的想法，我想创作一些宏大的东西，我想让这个，你知道，

sentences.en: big thing come to my mind, we have to understand how the brain really plays a role in creativity.
sentences.zh: 伟大的想法出现在我的脑海里”，我们必须了解大脑在创造力中扮演的角色。

sentences.en: So at the forefront of our creativity is the prefrontal cortex.
sentences.zh: 创造力的前沿是大脑的前额叶皮层。

sentences.en: You hear about this a lot, it's basically the biggest cortex, it's right at the front and it's responsible for decision making, abstract thinking and that is really what generates
